name: São Tomé
subtitle: São Tomé, capital of São Tomé and Príncipe: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 66,888 people lived in the City of São Tomé in the 2012 census (Água Grande District concentrates over 38% of the national population).
Founded in 1493 on Ana Chaves Bay, it was one of the earliest Atlantic plantation settlements powered by enslaved labor.
The 1575 Forte de São Sebastião houses the National Museum and commemorates the 1595 slave revolt led by Rei Amador.

parts.text: São Tomé was founded in 1493 by Portuguese captain Álvaro Caminha along the sheltered crescent of Ana Chaves Bay, growing into a pioneer sugar-plantation economy in the Gulf of Guinea.
In 1534, Pope Clement VII elevated its parish church to a cathedral, creating one of the earliest Catholic diocesan seats across sub-Saharan Africa.
Upon national independence in July 1975, the city became the sovereign capital of the Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe, embracing its rich Creole Forro language and culture.

blocks.prompt: About how many people were enumerated in the City of São Tomé in the 2012 census?

parts.text: 66,888 in the 2012 census by INE STP. The surrounding Água Grande District recorded 69,772 residents, representing nearly 40% of the archipelago's population.

items.text: Álvaro Caminha establishes the first permanent settlement on Ana Chaves Bay.
The Diocese of São Tomé is created by Pope Clement VII.
The stone fortress Forte de São Sebastião is completed at Ponta Sebastião.
Rei Amador leads a historic slave revolt, proclaiming himself king of the island.
São Tomé and Príncipe gains independence; São Tomé is declared capital.
The Museu Nacional opens inside the Forte de São Sebastião.
